newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-Swiss Re net jumps 33 pct to 1.46 bln Sfr.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Swiss Re net jumps 33 pct to 1.46 bln Sfr.

text.p: Swiss Re on Friday said 1996 net profit jumped 33 percent to 1.46 billion Swiss francs ($993 million), overshooting even optimistic forecasts for the world's second biggest reinsurer and the leader in life and health reinsurance.
"The 1996 business year was once again very satisfying for the Swiss Re group," the company said in a statement released after the Swiss stock exchange closed for the weekend.

Analysts cheered the news. "The profit is great. Capital has also developed excellently and that's the number I look at, because it influences future profits through investment," said analyst Heinrich-Horst Wiemer at CS First Boston.
Swiss Re registered shares closed earlier 40 Swiss francs higher at 1,746 in what traders called anticipation of a good financial scorecard.
Return on equity (ROE) was 13.8 percent after 12.7 percent in 1995, moving closer to a goal of 15 percent.
Swiss Re said its board of directors proposed raising the dividend to 30 francs from 22.50 on the basis of the 1996 gains and a "favourable assessment of current business trends."
It did not say anything more about the outlook for the current year, for which analysts have so far projected net profit between 1.45 billion and 1.6 billion.

Net profit after minority interests was 1.459 billion or 100 Swiss francs per share, well above widespread estimates of growth rates between 20 and 28 percent from a 1995 net of 1.10 billion or 75 francs per share.
"This increase is due mainly to continued improvement in technical results and a much higher return on investment activities," Swiss Re said.

Gross premiums were helped by currency fluctuations as the Swiss francs weakened last year, rising 11 percent to 14.2 billion Swiss francs when consolidated despite a decline of three percent in original currencies. Swiss Re said key balance sheet items were boosted by December's acquisition of Britain's Mercantile & General Re, which was consolidated in the balance at year-end but not on the profit and loss account.
Capital and reserves at balance sheet value increased by eight percent to 9.9 billion.
Technical provisions rose 46 percent from 1995 to 43.6 billion Swiss francs.
Investments at balance sheet value were 40 percent higher at 58.5 billion Swiss francs.
Swiss Re said investment profits rose 27 percent to 3,309 million Swiss francs in 1996 from the year before and return on investment grew to seven percent.
The technical result in life business rose 18 percent to 178 million.
The technical result in non-life business rose 19 percent to 716 million Swiss francs, the company said.
The combined ratio of claims and expenses to reinsurance premiums rose from 108 percent to 109 percent, including 435 million Swiss francs for provisions for catastrophe risks.
Swiss Re promised more detail on its 1996 results at a news conference and presentation to financial analysts on May 20.
A letter to shareholders and invitation to the annual general meeting would be sent out on May 5, Swiss Re said.
($ = 1.47 Swiss Francs)
